title: BROAD_MATCH quality publishes skos:closeMatch, and nothing says whether that is deliberate
body:
Surfaced while fixing the predicate contract in #694 (#390).

`sssom_grading.predicate_for()` special-cases exactly one asymmetric grade:

```python
if grade == "NARROW_MATCH":
    return PREDICATE_BROAD
if grade and grade not in EXACT_QUALITIES:
    return PREDICATE_CLOSE          # BROAD_MATCH lands here
```

So a record graded `BROAD_MATCH` — "this record is *broader* than its ontology term" — publishes `skos:closeMatch`, not an asymmetric predicate. Measured on the corpus: **1 record**.

The `review-sssom-output` skill said otherwise until #694 (`BROAD_MATCH` to `skos:broadMatch`), which is how this came to light: the documentation and the code disagreed, and the code has always done this.

Two readings, and I do not know which is intended:

- **Deliberate.** `closeMatch` is the conservative choice: it asserts no subclass edge at all, so a wrong `BROAD_MATCH` grade cannot make an ontology term a child of a MIM record. With one record in the corpus, conservative is defensible.
- **An omission.** `predicate_for` was written as a rule to stop `KeyError`s on grades the old table did not list (#525), and `BROAD_MATCH` simply fell into the default branch. Under SKOS the faithful predicate would be `skos:narrowMatch` — the object is the narrower concept — which is now rare-to-nonexistent in the corpus and so would stand out.

Not changed in #694 on purpose: moving it would turn one row from "informational, do not merge" into a `biolink:subclass_of` edge, which is a curation decision about that record rather than a contract correction.

**To close:** decide which reading is intended, record it next to `predicate_for`, and if it is an omission, review the one record before its predicate moves.
